name: Gana Fill

lead: Gana Fill is a PLLA-based injectable made in South Korea by GANA R&D. Rather than adding volume directly like a gel, a PLLA product is described as stimulating the body to produce collagen, so contour improves gradually after treatment.
Listings name the temples, cheeks, breasts and buttocks as treated areas and claim results lasting about two years; these are seller claims, and no independent trial of the product was found.

paras: It is supplied as a powder that a clinician mixes and injects; treatment is performed in clinic and results build over about two months according to one seller [1]. It is discussed in aesthetics and hardmaxxing circles as a volumising option for hollow temples and cheeks.

Fillers as a class can cause bruising, redness, pain and itching, and less commonly infection, allergic reaction, lumps or serious vascular complications [2]. Resellers sell the product online; regulatory approval details vary by market.

chain: Gradual restoration of volume in temples, cheeks or body areas
angle.text: Clients seek it to fill hollowing temples and cheeks or add body contour. Volume develops gradually as collagen forms rather than at the moment of injection.

lead: Gana Fill is an injectable poly-L-lactic acid (PLLA) product from the South Korean company GANA R&D, marketed under the GANAFill brand [1]. A seller listing describes it as a PLLA and hyaluronic acid powder that stimulates collagen formation to add volume, with listed areas including the temple, cheek, breasts and buttocks [1].

Collagen stimulators differ from standard hyaluronic acid fillers: PLA fillers work by stimulating collagen production instead of giving immediate volume [2]. The seller claims augmentation continues until about the eighth week and lasts about two years; these are unverified marketing claims [1].
The listing's "FDA approved materials" wording refers to ingredients and does not establish approval of the finished product [1]. No peer-reviewed study of Gana Fill was located.

paras: The seller listing identifies the product as injectable PLLA with hyaluronic acid powder, made in Korea, sold as "GANAFill" [1]. GANA R&D also markets other filler lines according to its own materials, which were not independently reviewed here.

PLA fillers (PLLA or PDLLA) are biodegradable polymers that stimulate collagen production instead of delivering immediate volume like hyaluronic acid [2]. Most wrinkle fillers are temporary and effects last about six months for common types [2].

Fillers commonly cause bruising, redness, pain and itching; less commonly infection or allergic reactions leading to lumps or scarring, and rarely vision loss from embolisation or delayed skin necrosis [2]. Regulation differs by market: in the US only a handful of fillers are FDA-approved devices, while in the EU and UK fillers carry a CE mark confirming production standards but not efficacy [2].
Collagen stimulators sit in the "hardmaxxing" category of clinic-delivered procedures. Gana Fill is sold by online resellers alongside other Korean fillers [1].
